Describe what changed between two extracts of a register

Source: R/describe_changes.R
describe_changes.Rd

A register is delivered again and again, and each delivery should differ from the last only where the world did: new persons, new years. When the same person-year has another birth date, sex or municipality than last time, a correction was made, and in the Greenlandic and Danish CPR, corrections have no time limit. describe_changes() compares two extracts by their key and counts the keys that came and went, the columns that came, went or changed type, and for every column the keys whose value changed, went missing or was filled in. It judges nothing.

Usage

describe_changes(old, new, ...)

Arguments

old, new

The earlier and the later extract: data frames, or two database tables on the same connection (see Database tables).

...

Key columns (tidy-select), e.g. cpr, year, present in both.

Value

An object of class inshape_changes, printed as a summary. It is a list with the counts n_old, n_new, n_kept (keys in both), n_added, n_removed and n_changed (kept keys with any changed column); columns_added, columns_removed and type_changed (column names); columns, a tibble with one row per shared column: column, changed (another value), went_missing (a value, now missing), filled_in (missing, now a value) and share (of the kept keys with any of the three), most changed first; and added and removed (the keys) and changed (the keys with n_columns, the number of columns that changed).

Details

Both extracts must be unique on the key; check with ensure_unique() or describe_key() first. Two missing values are equal. A column whose type changed, e.g. from integer to character, is compared as text, and integer and double columns as numbers.

Why it is fast

The keys of both extracts are compressed to integer ids together, by the compiled engine, so matching a row to its row in the other extract is an array lookup, with no join or sort. Each shared column is then compared in one compiled pass over the matched rows.

Database tables

Two dbplyr tables on the same connection, such as two DuckDB tables or two Parquet files read through DuckDB, are compared in the database: the counts are fetched, and added, removed and changed stay queries, to dplyr::collect() when needed.

See also

describe_key() to check the key first.

Examples

old <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "b", "c"), year = 2023,
                  sex = c("F", "M", "F"), born = c(1950, 1960, NA))
new <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "b", "d"), year = 2023,
                  sex = c("F", "F", "M"), born = c(1950, 1960, 1990))
# c is gone, d is new, and b changed sex
describe_changes(old, new, cpr, year)
#> ── Changes by cpr, year ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 3 rows before, 3 rows now, 2 keys in both
#> 
#> • New keys: 1 (33.3%)
#> • Keys gone: 1 (33.3%)
#> • Keys with a changed value: 1 (50.0%)
#> 
#> Changes per column, among the keys in both:
#>     column changed went_missing filled_in share 
#>   1 sex          1            0         0 50.00%
#>   2 born         0            0         0 0.00%
